content.thinking:
I'm reviewing the available build functions like joint, chain, sweep, loft, part, extrude, lathe, membrane, surface, decal, and stick, then starting to write the full implementation file using these.

Setting up imports and the skin and hair color palette, then thinking through how to add dramatic highlight shading to the hair with a lighter band effect.

Now I'm choosing the full color palette for the outfit pieces—tunic, cape, leather, gold trim—working out emerald, teal, and brown tones with appropriate shadow variants for each.

Writing skeleton builder code...

Setting up head joint attached to neck, then jaw hinge aimed toward the chin, ear joints on the head, and now defining clavicle joints attached to the chest.

Building the arm chains next, defining shoulder, elbow, and wrist joints as a polyline chain parented to each clavicle, though I'm weighing whether a sharp-cornered polyline is right versus a smoother curve for the elbow bend.

For legs, I'm using a dedicated limb helper that computes hip, knee, and ankle points given root/target positions, segment lengths, and a bend direction vector pointing the knee forward, then wiring those into a leg chain with contact points at the ankle.

For feet, I'm defining a short chain from the ball of the foot to the toe tip, parented off the ankle joint, so the foot pivots there when aimed toward the toe point.

For the foot shape itself, I'm sketching a sweep path from heel to ball to toe with tapering radii that narrow toward the toe, using rounded caps that extend slightly past the endpoints.

I realize the round caps add extra length, which would make the shoe too long for an elf's foot (around 0.27m), so I need to shorten the heel-to-toe span and adjust the ankle position accordingly.

Working out heel point at z≈0.0, with the cap radius pushing the back edge to roughly -0.045, and the toe tapering to z=0.185 extended by 0.03 for a total length near 0.255m, which fits better. Checking the ankle at y=0.115 against the boot radius confirms the foot-to-leg transition overlaps cleanly without gaps.

Now I'm thinking through the bone assignments for the foot sweep, wiring the chain references from the leg tip into the foot chain and checking that the heel path start lines up closely with the ankle joint. For the leg sweep, I'm using the hip-knee-ankle chain, and checking that the thigh radii leave just enough clearance at the crotch so the legs don't clip into each other.

For the head loft, I'm laying out the crown stations from top down, and working through how the "round" cap dome extends beyond the path end by the max radius -- I need the crown station positioned so the dome doesn't poke through the hair cap geometry, adjusting the width and height values to keep the dome radius in check.

Since the top of the cranium gets hidden under the hair cap anyway, I'm switching to a flat cap for that station instead, stacking down through wider stations toward the jaw, which ends in a rounded cap at the chin radius. Then for the nose, I'm sketching out a small tilted cone shape using a part with custom direction to angle it forward off the face.

For the mouth, I decide a curved catmull path is too fragile to sit exactly on the face surface, so I'm switching to a projected decal instead, using a small smile graphic positioned and sized to wrap naturally across the head and jaw geometry. Now I'm working out the hair cap as a scaled partial sphere to form an ellipsoid shape.

Continuing the hair geometry, I'm computing a second partial sphere for the side and back sections, carefully excluding the front sector angle so it doesn't overlap the face, and tuning the theta range so it blends smoothly with the first cap's coverage.

I'm checking that the exposed cheek skin near the sideburn edge stays uncovered since the hair bulges slightly outward there, and noting that since this is a single-sided partial sphere mesh, the open edge will appear hollow from certain viewing angles since the interior isn't rendered.

Now I'm placing the hair phi-cut caps so the bottom edge sits just above the eyes, forming overlapping forehead bangs, and planning the ear extrusion in code. For eyes, I'm positioning anime-style eye decals with iris color near the brow line, computing their size and angular offset from a center point on the face so they sit symmetrically at ±27° azimuth.

Moving on to arms, hands, bow, and quiver — I want to write the full file carefully, including boot lacing details. The cape will use a membrane attached to a spine bone joint, and I'll keep the color palette limited to a handful of flat colors for simplicity, with the bow rendered using a wood grain pattern along its length and a gold inlay accent on the limbs.

Writing bow band colors...

Now I'm working through the geometry of attaching hand to bow, computing shoulder and elbow joint positions for the left arm using direction vectors and lengths.

Still computing hand position coordinates...

Confirming no conflict with the arm since the tip curves down and stays clear of the wrist position. Checking the "left" convention stays consistent across views, then moving to compute the right arm's shoulder, elbow, and wrist coordinates using the same normalized direction vectors as before.

For the right hand, finger curl values look right for a relaxed hanging pose with a forward-inward palm, so natural curling direction works. Now I'm writing the hand function that takes wrist position, direction, palm normal, thumb direction, and curl arrays to compute finger joint positions...

Still working out finger geometry...

Working out the thumb joints now, with a base position offset from the wrist and two segments angled outward using blended direction vectors from curl rotation.

For the fist pose I want thumbCurl near 60° so it wraps over the grip, while an open hand uses a shallow 15°. I'm also setting slimmer radii for the thumb segments and deciding to skip nail geometry for now, instead focusing on building the bow shape from a Catmull-Rom spline through a set of control points with a radius function varying along its length.

Still shaping bow taper...

The bowstring stretches between the tips as a thin rod, with a nocking bead and serving detail at the string midpoint. I'm also adding gold tip caps, an emerald gem on the riser above the grip, and considering leaf-shaped gold fins on the riser, though I'll likely skip those for simplicity.

Now I'm working out the quiver geometry — defining its base and top points along the body, then building a lathed shell profile that tapers outward from the bottom, widens near the top, and closes back toward the axis to form an open-topped container shape, making sure the outline doesn't self-intersect.

Finishing the quiver's look, I'm setting up a leather paint pattern with gold trim bands near the top and a ring near the bottom based on surface position.

Now I'm placing seven arrows around the quiver opening, each offset slightly in the plane perpendicular to the central axis, with shafts rendered as rods running from a base point near the opening up through a fanned tilt at the top.

Still writing fletching details...

I need to check the arrow tops don't exceed head height, so I'm trimming the protrusion above the quiver rim to about 0.28 units, giving each shaft roughly 0.54 length with slight variation. The quiver also needs a small gold ring connecting to the shoulder strap, plus I'm considering whether to add a separate belt loop for stability.

For the baldric, I'm building the torso surface and defining a closed loop path of points around the chest that drapes toward the nearest surface point, then sweeping a thin box-section tube along it for the strap geometry. I'm also sketching a hip belt as a surface loop sampled around the torso.

I'm wrestling with the belt's sweep orientation though — the normal/binormal frame for a horizontal loop is ambiguous, so I need to figure out whether the radial thickness or vertical half-height corresponds to which axis, probably by testing with an explicit "up" vector and adjusting until the proportions look right in preview.

For the strap, buckle, and skirt panels I'll just build those directly and move on to writing out the full code, making sure the vector input types stay consistent between arrays and Vector3 objects.

Writing paint functions and gold colors...

Writing boot lacing paint logic...

Still writing SVG paths...

Scaling the mouth stroke for a 128px avatar, then positioning belt pouches and a dagger sheath using surface-hit placement around the torso.

Defining the dagged leaf-shaped tunic panels on each side with symmetric outlines, hem thickness, and tip positioning near the belt and thigh.

I'm correcting the tilt direction so the panel bottoms angle forward into the legs rather than back, adjusting the z-offset math accordingly, then planning the gold trim paint pattern along the panel edges.

Still designing dome geometry...

I'll attach the pauldron dome rigidly to the shoulderL bone since it swings with the arm, tilting its axis outward and upward to cover the shoulder, then layer smaller progressively tilted lames down along the upper arm direction.

For the paint, I'll give the dome a gold rim and radial leaf-vein ridges via lathe parameters, choosing a dark leather brown base to contrast with the teal cape and emerald tunic, plus a small glowing gem with a gold bezel at the dome top. I'll skip the clasp chain idea but still add a cream collar ring at the torso's shoulder yoke.

For the collar, I'm sweeping a closed ring around the neck with a cream tube and a thin gold lower line, then placing a gold leaf brooch with a gem and bezel at the front throat. I'm skipping the neckerchief and thigh garter bands, and deciding on a dark forest green for the pants to keep the green tones varied against the emerald tunic and teal cloak.

Settling on olive "#4b5d3f" for the pants alongside the emerald tunic, cream sleeves, brown leather accents, gold trim, and deep teal cloak, I'm now working out ear geometry, placing the root and tip points relative to the head to define their angle and curve.

Writing ear outline coordinates...

The cross product confirms the outline's +y points upward on the front, which is correct. I'm planning small gold stud earrings at the lobe position instead of a full ring/cuff setup, and adding hinge joints for the ears before extrusion so they can articulate. I'm also noting that head-based parts like the nose should reference the head bone, while jaw-based parts use the jaw bone.

For eye placement, I'll use surface hit retrieval against the combined head and jaw loft surfaces, sampling around a target point with azimuth and elevation angles to find the outermost hit. With the glow import path settled, I'm ready to write the final code to file, then typecheck and preview it.

input.command: ls scratch/elvenArcher samples | head; sed -n 1,60p src/decal.ts | head -80; grep -n "decal(" src/builder.ts
